detailed_description: The UUID Validator tool performs deep structural validation and metadata extraction of Universally Unique Identifiers (UUIDs) across versions 1-5. It verifies adherence to RFC 4122 standards by analyzing hexadecimal format, version-specific patterns, and variant identifiers. Technically, the tool parses the 36-character string into its five components (time_low, time_mid, time_high_and_version, clock_seq_and_variant, node), cross-checking each against the UUID specification. For version 1 UUIDs, it decodes the embedded timestamp (in 100-nanosecond increments since 1582) and MAC address. Version 3 and 5 validation includes checking MD5/SHA-1 namespace hashing. Developers need this tool to debug malformed UUIDs in distributed systems, validate API payloads, verify database entries, and ensure compliance during security audits. The analyzer also detects potential UUID collisions by examining node values and timestamp sequences, providing insights into generation patterns that could expose system vulnerabilities.
usage_steps: Enter the UUID string in the input field, which automatically highlights invalid characters in real-time
Select the expected UUID version (1-5) from the dropdown menu to enable version-specific validation
Click 'Validate' to trigger the parser, which dissects the UUID into its binary representation
Review the validation report showing format validity, version/variant compliance, and component breakdown
Expand the 'Timestamp Analysis' section to view decoded timestamps (version 1) or 'Namespace Check' for versions 3/5
Use the 'Export Results' button to download validation metadata in JSON format for automated testing pipelines
usage_examples: Verifying UUIDs in a REST API response to ensure they match version 4 generation requirements
Detecting version 1 UUIDs containing duplicate MAC addresses that expose internal network topology
Validating UUIDs in a NoSQL database to identify version mismatches causing data partition issues
Auditing version 5 UUIDs in a security token system to confirm proper SHA-1 namespace implementation
